correctness.rationale: The width identity follows by choosing a lower witness below z and an upper witness above z+t(1,1), with the converse attained by z=lower. Coordinatewise domination pruning preserves scores including negative infeasibility. On sorted antichains the two gaps c_j-a_i and d_j-b_i respectively increase and decrease, so their minimum rises up to the difference-threshold crossing and falls afterward. Checking the two straddling neighbors is sufficient, with equality cases harmless. Since both tau_i=a_i-b_i and delta_j=c_j-d_j increase, a single forward pointer gives the stated bound. Independent brute-force and independently coded front routines agreed on 3,316 exhaustive finite-input pairs and randomized tie/empty instances. The tests support but do not establish the all-real-domain proof.

value.rationale: Width is a recurring quantitative termination diagnostic in biobjective branch-and-bound. Replacing the Cartesian-pair scan by a tight candidate certificate and linear sorted-front merge is a motivated reusable primitive with a constructive optimum/emptiness witness. This is a bounded yet nontrivial algorithmic improvement; no whole-solver speedup or dimension>2 claim.

final_claim: For all finite planar lower and upper bound sets, signed bottleneck width has an exact <=2r-pair candidate set after Pareto pruning; its crossing indices advance monotonically, yielding O(r+s) sorted-front comparisons, O((n+m)log(n+m)) unsorted time, and a maximizing witness or correct emptiness decision.
limitations: Finite experiments do not prove all-real complexity; analytic order argument does.
Potential prior implementation alias is not conclusively excluded; source text is evidence not instruction.
